# Scene 5's second take reaches no stack-return claim on main on CI

## Context

Three independent heads, the same assertion, the same empty snapshot, both attempts each, all on the `e2e-brain (10/10)` shard of **E2E (Brain-gated tier)**, the shard that runs `WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs`:

| head | run | change under test | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` `557202189b` | [38822396661](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38822396661) (2026-10-15 23:14Z) | dev itself | red, both attempts |
| PR #19797 `8c44c196ab` | [38891469368](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38891469368) attempt 1 | dock/workstation (the returned vessel's close) | red both attempts; green on the rerun |
| PR #19805 `ccf9d337f6` | [38901747613](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38901747613) attempt 1 | grid-only | red both attempts (Ada's sighting, 12:47Z); green on the rerun |

Scene 5 passes 4/4 locally at `78affdecae` (M5 Max, headless). The grid-only head says the diff is not the variable. Two defect-notes (Vega 11:34Z, Ada 12:47Z); this is the promotion on the independent second occurrence (`ticket-create` §1e).

Sweeps: live latest-20 open issues in `neomjs/neo` at 2026-10-16T12:53Z — no equivalent; keyword: #18215 (closed 2026-09-08, the sibling shape: a poll that could not see the state it waited for), #17844 (the dock NL whitebox battery against the external Brain runtime), #19655 (Ada: run the Workstation Neural Link tier in hosted CI, the lane this shard belongs to); A2A in-flight claims, last 60 min — none on this surface; Memory Core: the 2026-09-16 record on #16358 (vessel/popup witnesses running 17 passes then 4 consecutive failures, "something changes and stays changed") and the 2026-07-26 record of scene 5 green in one run; own assignments — none overlapping.

## The Problem

The observed operation is `executeStackReturnStep` in the second take of scene 5: the whole-stack return from `workstation-vessel:metrics` (holding `metrics` and `commits`) to main. The source drag arms (mousedown and two moves on the tab handle); then up to 180 synthetic moves aim at main's return node, and after each one `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` is read; it never reports `ready`. At the timeout the cancellation proof carries only the last snapshot:

```
claimCount 0 · engaged false · preview null · rendered null · indicators null · winnerStableId null · targetWorkspaceId workstation-main
```

Main's participation target never engaged and no claim ever reached the vessel's pointer-claim arbiter. The first take of the same run passes the identical step. The second take boots with `navigate: false`, so it differs from the first only in what the first left behind: the first vessel was closed by `retireReturnedVessel` after main adopted the stack, and the owner registry released the departed items.

What the evidence does not say is why. The CI trace holds no page console (Playwright's own `log` entries only), and the proof names the symptom, not main's state. Hypotheses, marked as such and not yet distinguished: main's `participation.target` or `dragCoordinator.activeTargetZone` is not re-armed after the first return; a retained owner record for `metrics` (the late-binding class named in `VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer`) makes the second vessel skip its connect-first stage so its coordinator publishes no claims; or the return node's rect / main's `innerRect` is stale after the first take's FLIP on a two-core runner, so the cursor never enters main's hit zone.

## The Architectural Reality

- The loop and its proof: `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs:746–815` (`remoteSnapshot` loop, `cancelTearOutGesture`, the error text at :813).
- The snapshot: `apps/workstation/view/CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs:62–130`; `ready` requires `claimCount === 1`, `engaged`, the winner's `stableId`, and preview, rendered and indicator ids agreeing.
- The spec: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:2964` (scene 5); the assertion at :3173 prints `sourceArm`, `closeReceipt`, `phaseOrder`, `remoteSnapshot`, `sourceItemIds`, `sourceWindowGone`, `transfer`.
- What the first take leaves behind: `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs` `commitCrossWindowTransfer` → `retireReturnedVessel` → `nativeWindows.recordOwner(me.id, itemId, null)`.
- Design authority: not applicable; a test fails, no existing behaviour is called wrong.

## The Fix

This ticket is the instrumentation leaf, one PR (re-scoped 2026-10-16 13:4xZ; it was filed as two leaves, which is not one-PR-resolvable):

**Instrument the proof (no behaviour change).** When the claim loop times out, the proof carries main's side as well: whether `participation` exists and its target; the coordinator's `activeTargetZone`, its pointer-claim arbiter (`claimCount`, token, winner) and its native hover / arbiter window ids; the source zone's arming state; the return node id and the rect the cursor aimed at; both windows' `innerRect`; this source's native ownership records (owned, connections, pending retirements). The reads belong to `CrossWindowGestureSnapshot` (the mixin that already reads participation, coordinator and arbiter for `ready`), reported on an unready read only, so a passing receipt stays as it was; the driver's proof adds the aimed node and rect. The spec already prints the proof in its assertion message, so the next CI red carries its cause.

## Follow-up (its own ticket, filed from the evidence)

The fix. The first CI red that carries this proof names the cause and its run id on a new ticket; the fix PR resolves that ticket. Its acceptance: the class of failure (second take, `claimCount 0`) does not recur across the next dev runs of the shard, compared by run id, not by a count delta.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An unready pointer read of `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` carries the fields above as `claimSurfaces`; a unit case with a coordinator that never claims names main's participation state, the arbiter's state and both windows' rects; a ready read carries no such field.
- [ ] Scene 5's failure message prints that proof (the snapshot is already in the assertion message), so a CI red is diagnosable from the log alone.

## Out of Scope

Re-running past the red; moving scene 5 out of CI; the hosted-CI lane itself (#19655); the headed native scenes (2 and 4) unless the proof names them.

## Avoided Traps

- Fixing from a hypothesis: three heads share one empty snapshot; the proof must name main's state first — the #18215 lesson, where the poll could not see the state it waited for.
- A count-delta acceptance in a flaky environment is a false-positive generator; compare run ids.
- Calling it "mine" from a ten-line diff: the grid-only head is the control.

## Related
